successors.name: Sasanian Empire
successors.text: Persian Armenia (Persarmenia): in 428 Bahram V 'abolished the Kingdom of Armenia and appointed Veh Mihr Shapur as marzban'

successors.name: Eastern Roman Empire
successors.text: the smaller Roman share, 'Sophene and a smaller portion of Armenia', west of the line from Erzurum to Mush

ledger.x: 331: Orontes III's Armenia emerges from the Achaemenid collapse.
321: the satrapy becomes a kingdom.

c. 260: Sophene becomes a separate kingdom. Orontid infobox 'Founded ... 260 BC (Sophene)', with 'Sames of Sophene (c. 260 BC) and Arsames I (260–228 BC)'. The same page says 'Towards the end of 212 BC the country was divided into two kingdoms, both vassal states of the Seleucids'; Cliopatria separates Sophene in 256…
210: the capital moves from Armavir to Yervandashat.
200: Artaxias I overthrows Orontes IV; the Artaxiad dynasty replaces the Orontids.
176: the capital moves to Artaxata (Artashat).

c. 110: the east is lost to Parthia. The Tigranes page dates no loss in 110; the date is the Cliopatria change (224,379 to 132,054 km2, east edge from 48.93 to 44.87 E). The parthian-empire dossier has Armenia a Parthian vassal from 120. Bridging judgment: the page has Tigranes 'a hostage at the Parthian court until…

c. 95: Tigranes cedes the 'seventy valleys'. 'Tigranes ceded an area called "seventy valleys" in the Caspiane to Mithridates II' when released c. 96/95 (page); 'When he acquired power, he recovered these valleys'. The page does not date the cession itself; the year is the release. The valleys lie in the east, probably…

c. 95: Sophene is absorbed. 'He deposed Artanes, the last king of the Kingdom of Sophene' (Tigranes page, undated); the Orontid page's infobox gives Sophene's 'Dissolution: 95 BC' and the kingdom-of-sophene dossier uses 95.
87: Atropatene is retaken.
87: Gordyene is retaken, in the same sentence ('Between 88 and 85 BC').
87: Adiabene is retaken, in the same sentence ('Between 88 and 85 BC').
83: Tigranes becomes king of Syria.
77: the capital moves to the new city of Tigranocerta.

c. 77: the rest of the empire. Cliopatria's 77 outline (519,631 km2) is about 130,000 km2 larger than the 87 outline plus the Seleucid rump. The Artaxiad page says only: 'Large territories were taken from the Parthians, who were forced to sign a treaty of friendship with Tigranes' and 'Iberia, Albania, and Atropatene…
69: the capital returns to Artaxata after Tigranocerta falls.
69: Syria slips away and a Seleucid rump is restored.
69, 6 October: Lucullus beats Tigranes at Tigranocerta.
66: Tigranes surrenders to Pompey.
66: the empire is stripped.
63: the outline widens again in the west.
34: Mark Antony invades Armenia.
34: the invasion is over in the year it began; the pages record the defeat of the kingdom and nothing later until Augustus's 20 BC truce with Parthia, which made Armenia 'a buffer zone'.
12: the last Artaxiad kings are overthrown ('overthrown in 12 AD', Kingdom page lead); the Arsacid page has 'The first appearance of an Arsacid on the Armenian throne occurred in 12' (Vonones I).

52: Tiridates I founds the Arsacid dynasty of Armenia (Kingdom page: Tiridates I is proclaimed king in 52 AD, founding the Arsacid dynasty); the Roman-Parthian War page has the Parthians installing him 'in 52/53' and Armenia a Roman client of Nero's from the 66 coronation.
58: Rome and Parthia fight over Armenia.
63: the Treaty of Rhandeia (Kingdom page): Arsacid members rule Armenia as Roman client kings; Tiridates went to Rome and was crowned by Nero in 66.
114: Trajan annexes Armenia.
118: Hadrian gives Armenia up.
120: the capital moves to Vagharshapat.
161: Vologases IV invades Armenia.
164: Rome reinstalls its king.
252: the Sasanian Persians occupy Armenia (Kingdom page, 252 AD); 'after which Shapur laid waste to the country' (Arsacid page, after Barbalissos, c.

287: Tiridates III returns with Roman armies (Kingdom page, 287 AD: he is brought to power by Roman armies; the infobox gives his reign as 298-330 and the Narseh page restores him only after Satala; the sasanian-empire dossier has the loss in 299).
298/9: the Peace of Nisibis.
336: the capital moves to Dvin.
368: Shapur II conquers Armenia.
370/371: Pap restores the kingdom.
387: Armenia is partitioned between Rome and Persia.
387: the eastern strip that Cliopatria's 387 shape drops (to 47.12 E) falls with the Persian share.
428: the Arsacid kingdom is abolished.

wars.name: Antiochus III's campaign in Armenia and Sophene
wars.outcome: Antiochus III besieged Arsamosata; Xerxes of Sophene and Commagene surrendered and the country was divided into two kingdoms, both Seleucid vassals.

wars.name: Tigranes the Great's conquests
wars.outcome: Tigranes retook Adiabene, Gordyene and Media Atropatene (88-85), then took the Seleucid rump in 83 and 'conquered Phoenicia and Cilicia'; his empire reached from the Caspian to the Mediterranean.

wars.name: Third Mithridatic War, Roman invasions of Armenia
wars.outcome: Lucullus beat Tigranes at Tigranocerta (6 October 69) and reached Artaxata (6 October 68); Pompey forced his surrender in 66 and left him Armenia 'shorn of his conquests' for 6,000 talents.

wars.name: Mark Antony's invasion of Armenia
wars.outcome: Antony invaded and defeated the kingdom in 34 BC and sent Artavasdes II to Egypt, where he was executed.

wars.name: Roman-Parthian War of 58-63
wars.outcome: Rome marched on Tigranocerta in 59, lost the Battle of Rhandeia in 62, and in 63 the settlement made the Arsacid Tiridates a Roman client king; he was crowned by Nero in Rome in 66.

wars.name: Trajan's annexation of Armenia
wars.outcome: Trajan deposed Parthamasiris and made Armenia a Roman province in 114; Hadrian gave it up in 118 and installed Parthamaspates.

wars.name: Roman-Parthian War of 161-166
wars.outcome: Vologases IV invaded Armenia in 161; Statius Priscus took Artaxata in 163 and Sohaemus was installed in 164; Rome then went down the Euphrates to Dura-Europos and sacked Ctesiphon and Seleucia (165), the war ending in 166 with Roman gains in upper Mesopotamia.

wars.name: Sasanian conquest of Armenia
wars.outcome: The Sasanian Persians occupied Armenia in 252, after Barbalissos; Armenia stayed under Iranian rule until Tiridates III's restoration (287 or 298/9).

wars.name: Roman-Sasanian war of 296-298
wars.outcome: Galerius beat Narseh at Satala in 298; the Peace of Nisibis (298/9) gave Rome five provinces beyond the Tigris, extended Armenia to Zintha in Media and Tiridates III was reinstated.

wars.name: Shapur II's conquest of Armenia
wars.outcome: Shapur II laid waste to Armenia and held Arshak II captive; Pap regained the throne with Valens's help in 370/371.

wars.name: Partition of Armenia between Rome and Persia
wars.outcome: Persia received the larger share (Persarmenia), Rome Sophene and a smaller portion, on a line from Erzurum to Mush.

certainty.note: Armenian frontiers are known from historians and the Roman-Parthian settlements, not from survey lines; the Tigris-side districts after the 298/9 peace and Rome's border at the Euphrates were negotiated but their lines are not on the pages.
The Roman-Persian line 'from Erzurum to Mush' (387) is the only treaty-drawn frontier on the pages and could be drawn sharply as a segment; every other edge stays soft.
